how_to_apply: Read the instructions in the advertisement, then fill the prescribed form attached to it, in clean and clear handwriting of your own.
Paste a recent passport-size photograph, not older than 3 months, on the form.
Attach the documents listed below and complete the declaration.
Submit the form during office hours at one of these Sub Divisional Officer (Police) offices: Bhairamgarh, Kutru, Farsegarh, Bhopalpatnam or Awapalli.
If applying by post, use registered Indian Post only and address it to the Office of the Superintendent of Police, District Bijapur, PIN No. 494444.
Make sure a posted form reaches the Superintendent of Police office, Bijapur, by the last date during office hours. Forms received later will not be accepted.

content_sections.heading: Bijapur Police Bastar Fighter Constable Vacancy Details 2026
content_sections.text: The number of posts and the pay scale may be increased or reduced under instructions issued from time to time by the State Government and Police Headquarters, Nava Raipur. Ex-servicemen: 10% of vacancies. Local women of Bijapur district: 30% of posts, as horizontal reservation under the Chhattisgarh Civil Services (Special Provisions for Appointment of Women) rules. Home Guards: 25% horizontal reservation, as per the rules. Assistant Constables: 15% horizontal reservation. Former Agniveers: 10% horizontal and category-wise reservation, under the Chhattisgarh Government letter dated 14 October 2026. State Government instructions and rules issued from time to time apply to all reservation.

rows.pay: Pay Matrix Level-4 as approved by the government, plus allowances payable from time to time

content_sections.heading: Bijapur Police Bastar Fighter Constable Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates must be not less than 18 years and not more than 28 years old on 1 January 2026. SC, ST and OBC candidates: upper age limit relaxed by a maximum of 5 years. Local women of Bijapur district: upper age limit relaxable up to 10 years, under the Chhattisgarh Civil Services (Special Provisions for Appointment of Women) Rules, 1997. Current or former Chhattisgarh Government employees not declared unfit for government service may get relaxation on the conditions below. Permanent government servants must not be more than 36 years old. Candidates holding a temporary post and applying for another post must not be more than 36 years old. This concession also covers employees paid from the contingency fund, work-charged employees and those working under project implementation committees. Retrenched government servants may deduct their full earlier temporary service from their age, up to a maximum of 7 years, even if it was served on more than one occasion. The resulting age must not exceed the upper age limit by more than 3 years. All age concessions are subject to the Chhattisgarh Government's guidelines. 10th class pass from a school located in Chhattisgarh or Madhya Pradesh. Scheduled Tribe candidates are eligible with a 5th class pass. Candidates of all categories from Naxal-affected families in the state, or from families living in relief camps in Naxal-affected areas, are eligible with a 5th class pass. The qualification must be held on the last date for submitting applications. Attaching the qualification certificate with the form is the applicant's own responsibility. Candidates of every category must show at least 5 cm chest expansion. Women candidates are exempt from this standard. The selection committee's decision on height and chest measurement is final. The candidate must not be physically disabled and must be medically fit. Knock-knee and flat-foot are not allowed. The candidate must not have any eye disease and must be able to distinguish the primary colours. The competent authority will examine such cases personally and may consult the District Chief Medical Officer if needed. Third gender candidates follow the male standards if their certificate states male and the female standards if it states female, and must produce that certificate. The official notification gives the full eligibility conditions for this post.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Selection takes place in stages, starting with document verification and physical measurement. Separate dates will be issued for each stage. Candidates get only one chance in each event, and taking part in all events is compulsory. Unreserved candidates must score 60 percent of the 100 marks. SC, ST and OBC candidates must score 50 percent. A candidate unhappy with the assessment of their performance may appeal to the selection committee, which will settle it immediately. Its decision is final. Written examination: a maximum of 15 times the number of advertised posts will be called. Interview: a maximum of 3 times the number of advertised posts will be called. All candidates with the same cut-off marks are included at both stages. The final merit list is prepared from the combined marks in the physical efficiency test, written examination and interview, plus any bonus marks earned.

faq.question: Q1. Can a 5th pass candidate apply for the Bastar Fighter Constable post?
faq.answer: Yes, if the candidate belongs to a Scheduled Tribe, or to a Naxal-affected family or a family living in a relief camp in a Naxal-affected area. Other candidates need a 10th pass from a school in Chhattisgarh or Madhya Pradesh.

faq.question: Q2. Can someone from outside Bijapur district apply?
faq.answer: No. The form asks whether the candidate is a local resident of the district, and a certificate from the competent authority must be attached.

faq.question: Q3. What is the height requirement for Scheduled Tribe candidates?
faq.answer: Scheduled Tribe men need 150 cm or more and Scheduled Tribe women need 148 cm or more.

faq.question: Q4. Do women candidates have to meet the chest measurement?
faq.answer: No. Women candidates are exempt from the chest standard, but they must still meet the height and medical standards.

faq.question: Q5. How many marks are needed to clear the physical efficiency test?
faq.answer: Unreserved candidates need 60 percent of the 100 marks, and SC, ST and OBC candidates need 50 percent.

faq.question: Q6. Which skill gives the most bonus marks?
faq.answer: Knowledge of the district's local dialect gives 20 of the 30 possible bonus marks, far more than the 5 marks each for a heavy licence or an NCC or NSS "C" certificate.

faq.question: Q7. Can a serving government employee apply?
faq.answer: Yes. A permanent government servant must not be more than 36 years old, and government, semi-government, and state corporation or board employees must attach a no-objection certificate from their head of department.

faq.question: Q8. Why must I keep the postal receipt?
faq.answer: Candidates who send the form by registered post must bring the receipt with them on the date fixed for recruitment. This is compulsory.
